attributionRule.edgeSideMembership: existing branch path of the edge source
attributionRule.nodeSideMembership: existing branch path of the intruded node
attributionRule.directAttribution: source and node paths each contain exactly one token for focus fork f, and those tokens name opposite yes/no immediate children

conclusion.sourceTargetDisagreementInterpretation: Jumps and reentries often end outside the source branch. Target paths cannot replace source paths wholesale, but they expose the direct-departure blind spot.
conclusion.counterexample: At focus i-53, edge i-53-yes semantically departs the yes child while i-54 is in i-53/no; the source node i-53 has no i-53 child token, so source-path attribution incorrectly leaves the event unattributed.
conclusion.stopReason: Source-path attribution is insufficient for a direct focus-fork departure, so the counterexample discipline stops before changing orientation scoring.
